# Titles and rows

What a terminal’s title says after its name, and what its row in the list says on its second line, are two templates in the settings: `appearance.titleFormat` and `appearance.rowFormat`. They are changed in Settings → Appearance, Titles and rows (the command “Titles and rows: what they show”), or written by hand in `config.json`. The title’s template is drawn on the canvas and at the head of a terminal in a browser tab of its own; the row’s on the second line of a row (a row of one line, “One line per terminal”, says its state alone, beside the name).

## The language

A template is one line of at most 200 characters, without control characters: text, with placeholders in braces. `{{` and `}}` are a brace. The name always comes first and is not part of a template, so `{name}` is not a placeholder.

- Text is drawn as it is written, as text: a template carries no markup and no style.
- A placeholder is drawn the way the page draws that thing everywhere else: the state in the color of that state, a link as a chip, a field’s value with any address in it as a chip, the step of a run pressed for the run.
- A placeholder that is not known, is not for that place, or is a `{field:}` without a label is said in Settings, under the field, and skipped; the rest is still drawn. A `{` that is not closed is said too, and the template is not saved until it is.
- A template in the file that is not one as a whole (not text, too long, more than one line) is the default, by itself.

## What hangs from a placeholder

A placeholder with nothing to say is left out, and so is the text that would hang from it:

> Text after a placeholder is drawn only when that placeholder said something and a later one does too; text before the first placeholder only when the first said something; text after the last only when the last said something. A template with no placeholder is drawn as written, and text that is only spaces draws nothing of its own.

So `{state} · {step} · {time}` never shows a dot with nothing on one side of it. On a row, two pieces with nothing written between them have the row’s own quiet dot between them; text written between them stands there instead.

## What stays as it is

Whatever a template says: the name comes first, and in a title the dot of its state before it; the title is one row that never wraps and the row’s second line one line; the name gives way first, then the marks, and a state is never cut; the tools at the end of a title (Note, Details, Tab, the menu) stay at its right end; text is in the sizes of the page.

## The placeholders

| Placeholder | Where | Drawn as | What it says |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{state}` | title, row | the state | Its state in words where it is not the ordinary one, in that state’s color: waiting for you, finished; on a row also working and a failed exit. |
| `{exit}` | title | a mark | How its last command ended, where it failed: exit 2. |
| `{untold}` | title | a mark | That a sentence could not be typed for its agent lately: not told. |
| `{messages}` | title | a mark | Its messages, where some are unread or for you: pressed to read them. |
| `{activity}` | title, row | words | What it is doing: the command running now, else the program and its folder. |
| `{command}` | title, row | words | What runs: the command running now, else the program it was started with, short; the whole line when pointed at. |
| `{folder}` | title, row | words | Its folder, the last two parts; the whole path when pointed at. |
| `{step}` | title, row | a step | The step of the run it is on, and how many there are: pressed for the whole run. |
| `{copy}` | title | a mark | The working copy it works in: its branch and how many files changed, pressed for what changed. |
| `{list}` | title, row | a mark | A list its agent handed in, and how much of it is ticked: pressed to open it. |
| `{standing}` | title, row | words | Whether it is parked or its shell has ended, and the agent a terminal read in from a file was meant for. |
| `{time}` | title, row | a time | When it was last typed into or last printed, whichever is later: 4m ago. |
| `{typed-by}` | title, row | a mark | Which API token typed into it last: in a title for half a minute, on a row with the time. |
| `{desktop}` | title | a mark | That something outside the page shows it too, most likely a window of your terminal application: also on desktop. |
| `{resume}` | title | a mark | Resume agent, where its agent can be started again in the conversation it was last in. |
| `{people-only}` | title, row | a mark | That no API token may read it or type into it: people only. |
| `{links}` | title | link chips | The marks of at most three of its links, the ticket and the pull request first: each pressed to open. |
| `{tags}` | title, row | tags | Its tags: in a title the first and how many more, pressed to change them; on a row each one, pressed to list only those. |
| `{canvas}` | title, row | words | The name of the canvas it is on. |
| `{project}` | title, row | words | The name of its project. |
| `{theme}` | title, row | words | The name of the color theme its body is drawn in. |
| `{agent}` | title, row | words | The agent on record in it: the program seen in front when it last reported, else its kind. |
| `{branch}` | title, row | words | The branch of its folder, as found by looking there. |
| `{pull-request}` | title, row | a link chip | The pull request of that branch, where the gh tool told one: a chip, pressed to open it. |
| `{field:<label>}` | title, row | a field | The value of its field with that label, whatever the capitals: {field:Ticket}. An address in it is a chip. |

## The defaults

They draw what a title and a row drew before there were templates:

- Title: `{state} {exit} {untold} {messages} {activity} {copy} {list} {typed-by} {desktop} {resume} {people-only} {links} {tags}`
- Row: `{state} {step} {standing} {time} {people-only} {typed-by} {tags}`

## Examples

- A title that says where it works and its ticket: `{state} {folder} · {field:Ticket} {links} {tags}`
- A row that says its folder and its branch: `{state} {step} {folder} · {branch} {time}`
- A row with words between: `{state} on {canvas}, {time}`. With nothing to say on its canvas, it reads `waiting for you`, not `waiting for you on ,`.
